name: Banana Islands
subtitle: The Banana Islands, south of Freetown, comprise Dublin, Ricketts and a small uninhabited island.

facts.label: Location
facts.value: Dublin, the capital, stands 33 km south of Freetown

facts.label: Islands
facts.value: Dublin, Ricketts (joined to Dublin by a causeway) and a small uninhabited island

facts.label: Population (2006)
facts.value: About 500 people, many obliged to find work in Freetown

facts.label: Livelihoods
facts.value: Most inhabitants subsist on farming and fishing

facts.label: Civil war
facts.value: Sheltered some 5,000 refugees during the civil war

facts.label: Early history
facts.value: First invaded by 16th-century Portuguese navigators, followed by British slave traders

facts.label: Slave trade
facts.value: A local historian says John Newton built the fortress where captives were held (local account)

parts.text: The Banana Islands, south of Freetown, comprise Dublin, Ricketts and a small uninhabited island. A 2006 report put the population at about 500, living mainly by farming and fishing. The islands were used in the slave trade and sheltered some 5,000 refugees during the civil war.

gaps: The description is summarised from the sources listed here and should be read against them.
